## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Nandakattheraapadāna* (Tha Ap 408) is a verse narrative in the Therāpadāna section of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya recounting the past-life deeds and spiritual biography of the elder Nandaka [SuttaCentral]. In an analysis of the distribution and chronology of Pali aorist forms, Paul Kingsbury identifies Apadāna 408 as exhibiting notable clustering or priming effects in verbal morphology, pointing out that seven of the nine canonical attestations of the thematic aorist *sannipatuṃ* occur in successive verses of this specific text [Kingsbury 2002].

According to text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus, the text shares extensive material across the Pali corpus. Its closest reuse partners include the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā* and the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, as well as numerous formulaic verses shared with other Apadāna poems, particularly the *Ekachattiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 414), another homonymous *Nandakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 547), and the *Padumakūṭāgāriyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 397) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language machine alignments by DharmaNexus also detect shared narrative or thematic segments in the Chinese *Saṃyuktāgama* (Taishō 99) and the Tibetan version of the *Bodhisattvāvadānakalpalatā* [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records no curated external parallels, but lists five translations across five modern languages [SuttaCentral].
